name: apple-pdf-mcp
description: Full PDFKit read/write access — text, search, page assembly, annotations, forms, encryption, metadata, rendering and redaction
long_description:
A local MCP server written in Swift for full PDF interaction through PDFKit — not just extracting text. Reading: text page by page, the bookmark outline, document metadata, full-text search, listing existing annotations and form fields. Writing: page assembly (merge, reorder, extract, split, delete, rotate), adding/removing/searching-and-highlighting annotations, filling AcroForm fields (with optional flattening), encryption and permissions, metadata editing, page rendering to PNG, and redaction.

Every tool that changes a PDF writes its result to a new path and never touches the file(s) it read.

pdf_redact_pages is worth understanding before use: it does not merely paint over the given rectangles, which would leave the original text extractable underneath. It rasterizes each affected page whole after painting, replacing it with a plain image — a redacted page loses its entire text layer, not just the redacted area. That is the only way public PDFKit makes redaction genuinely irreversible; there is no middle option.

Two things public PDFKit cannot do, so this server does not pretend to: a real cryptographic signature (no public API attaches one), and redaction without the whole-page rasterization trade-off above.

A PDF with no text layer at all is a scan. This server says so explicitly instead of returning empty pages rather than guessing; reading the pixels is text recognition, which this server does not do.

The two folder lists below are the ONE deliberate exception to "nothing to configure": together they are the security boundary itself, not a preference, so there is no sensible default to hardcode in their place. Leaving either blank means nothing is reachable through it; guessing one would mean guessing what may be exposed. Being allowed to read a folder's PDFs does not by itself allow writing into it — the lists are independent.

A password-protected PDF is refused by every read tool unless the correct password is given as that tool's own argument; the write tools do not accept a password for their input yet.

Not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.

tools.name: pdf_status
tools.description: Reports which folders this server may read from and write into, and whether macOS is actually letting it reach them. Reads no file contents.

tools.name: pdf_read
tools.description: Extracts text from a PDF with PDFKit, page by page, plus its outline (bookmarks) and document metadata — title, author, subject, keywords, producer and dates. outline_query searches the outline by title instead of returning it whole, which matters once it runs to hundreds of entries.

tools.name: pdf_search
tools.description: Finds every occurrence of a string in a PDF and returns each hit's page number plus the full line it appears on. Case- and accent-insensitive by default, so "resume" and "résumé" match each other.

tools.name: pdf_list_annotations
tools.description: Lists every annotation already on a PDF — highlights, notes, shapes, links, form widgets — with its page, type, contents and position.

tools.name: pdf_list_form_fields
tools.description: Lists every AcroForm field in a PDF, with its name, kind, current value and whether it is read-only.

tools.name: pdf_merge_pages
tools.description: Builds a new PDF by copying pages from one or more sources, in order -- merges, reorders, extracts/splits or deletes pages depending on what is passed. Never modifies a source.

tools.name: pdf_rotate_pages
tools.description: Rotates specific pages of a PDF by a multiple of 90 degrees and writes the result to a new file. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_add_annotation
tools.description: Adds a highlight, underline, strike_out, note, free_text or square/circle annotation to a page and writes the result to a new file. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_remove_annotation
tools.description: Removes one annotation (addressed as pdf_list_annotations reports it) and writes the result to a new file. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_highlight_text
tools.description: Finds every occurrence of a string and adds a Highlight annotation over each one, then writes the result to a new file. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_fill_form
tools.description: Sets values on a PDF's AcroForm fields by name and writes the result to a new file. Optionally flattens the form permanently. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_set_password
tools.description: Encrypts a PDF with a user and/or owner password and a permission list, and writes the result to a new file. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_remove_password
tools.description: Unlocks a PDF with a password and writes a plain, unencrypted copy. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_set_metadata
tools.description: Sets title, author, subject and/or keywords on a PDF's metadata and writes the result to a new file. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_render_page
tools.description: Renders one page to a PNG image, exactly as it displays. Never modifies the source.

tools.name: pdf_redact_pages
tools.description: Genuinely redacts given rectangles on given pages by rasterizing each affected page whole, then writes the result to a new file. Never modifies the source.

read_roots.title: Folders Claude may read
read_roots.description: Claude can open any PDF inside these. Nothing outside them is reachable.

write_roots.title: Folders Claude may write
write_roots.description: Claude can save new or edited PDFs and images inside these. Being able to read a folder's PDFs does not by itself allow writing into it — leave this blank to keep the server read-only.
